meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (PRC) as the WFOE formation domicile, with Taiwan as the investor-origin jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (socialist legal system with Chinese characteristics)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 13 September 2024, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Ownership Information (Order No. 3 [2024] of the People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (revised 2023, effective 1 July 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (as amended) for the investor-origin documentary integrity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan shareholder/investor (company registration certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, Company Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public notarization; then verified by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and forwarded through the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait (ARATS) to the PRC competent authorities. This is the mandatory cross-strait authentication route; Hague Apostille is inapplicable because the PRC does not recognize Taiwan as an Apostille Convention state, and Consular Legalization is inapplicable because no PRC consulate operates in Taiwan.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or current registration information certificate of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan, Company Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same cross-strait SEF/ARATS notarization and verification path; not Hague Apostille and not Consular Legalization; the two authentication methods are parallel and mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution and irrevocable Power of Attorney authorizing establishment of the China WFOE and execution of all statutory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investor, notarized by a Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by Taiwan notary; authenticated by the Taiwan court clerk; verified by SEF and forwarded to ARATS; no Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization is to be added sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) of the Taiwan investor, in its current consolidated and registered version
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan investor, attested by the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-strait verification through SEF/ARATS after Taiwan notarization; Hague Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (relationship, creditworthiness, and AML compliance attestation) for the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank (issuing branch or head office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature confirmed before a Taiwan notary public; then SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification; not a Hague Apostille and not a Consular Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the WFOE counsel must screen every shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, director, supervisor, senior manager, authorized signatory, and beneficial owner of the Taiwan investor against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions, EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions, PBOC adverse AML lists, PRC MOFCOM export control and sanction lists, the Supreme People's Court judgment debtor and dishonest person list, and the domestic PEP database covering senior officials, their family members and close associates, including Taiwan-listed persons. Screening must be refreshed every 90 days and on any ownership event. All matches must be escalated to the compliance committee and documented through a risk-based enhanced due diligence file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration and Self-Service Declaration System of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), operated through the provincial and municipal Market Supervision Administration integrated online platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered Chinese name must be composed entirely of simplified Chinese characters and must follow the four-tier statutory format: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name, which may be the transliteration of the foreign investor's Chinese name; (3) industry or business characteristics reflecting commercial legal services; and (4) company legal form as limited liability company. The English name, if used, must be a faithful translation and must be filed together with the Chinese name; Pinyin-only names are not accepted as the statutory Chinese name. Foreign-language names may appear only as ancillary translations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receipt of the SAMR name-rejection notice, the applicant may either apply to the next-higher market supervision authority for administrative reconsideration within 60 days from the date of receipt, or directly initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. If the reconsideration path is chosen, a further judicial review may be available within 15 days after the reconsideration decision. In parallel, counsel should immediately revise and refile the name through the same enterprise name self-service system, removing any objectionable token or obtaining the required ministerial approval. A written appeal book, citing the applicable enterprise name registration rules and explaining the distinctiveness of the requested name, must accompany the reconsideration application. If the 30-day reservation expires, a new reservation must be filed; extension is not automatic and must be requested before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices and commercial mailboxes are rejected for this WFOE. SAMR requires the registered address to be a fixed, physical business site; the local tax authority requires a lease contract, landlord real-estate certificate, and utility receipts; banks opening the IOLTA trust account will treat virtual addresses as a lack of commercial substance and will refuse KYC clearance. Co-working space may be accepted only if it is a dedicated office under a registered sublease with on-site employee presence during business hours, business signage, and a reception function. The legal-services licensing authority will also conduct a pre-authorization inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified likelihood: 60 percent probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the local SAMR or tax authority within the first 12 months of incorporation. Checklist: physical receipt of official mail, display of business license, company nameplate, employment records, social insurance payment records, lease and landlord consent, property ownership certificate, utility bills, attendance records, client files maintained confidentially, IOLTA ledger segregation, and internal AML/CFT procedures. Higher-risk triggers include a residential address, absence of personnel, non-matching lease, failure to pay rent or utilities, and inconsistent beneficial-owner disclosure. If inspection fails, the registration may be revoked and the company blacklisted.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended, particularly Articles 1-10, 128-130, 156-160 (incorporation, shares, capital), and the Foreign Investment Act (Act No. 1 of 1954, as amended) for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (MOEA) - Company Registration Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration (Form 1) together with the Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a WFOE in Taiwan; however, the capital must be sufficient to cover initial operating expenses and must be remitted from abroad and deposited in a local bank account before incorporation. The Investment Commission may require a capital plan commensurate with the business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Board shall issue and subscribe 1,000,000 ordinary shares of NT$10 each to the sole shareholder, [Shareholder Name], at par value, and that the subscription shall be credited to the Company's capital account upon receipt of the full consideration in cash or in kind as approved by the Board.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board hereby authorizes the Chairman and the Managing Director, jointly and severally, to open and maintain bank accounts with any reputable financial institution in Taiwan, to sign all banking opening documents, to execute all banking agreements, and to operate such accounts for the purpose of the Company's business, including but not limited to the deposit of capital contributions and the withdrawal of funds for operational expenses.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [Address], Taiwan, and that the Company shall file all necessary notices with the Ministry of Economic Affairs to record this address as the statutory registered office.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are hereby appointed as the first statutory officers of the Company: [Name] as Chairman of the Board, [Name] as Managing Director, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting or until their successors are duly elected and qualified.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairman and the Managing Director are authorized to execute all documents, to make all filings, and to take all necessary actions to effectuate the incorporation of the Company, including the execution of the Articles of Incorporation and the submission of the incorporation application to the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company adopts the Articles of Incorporation as presented to this Board, and that the same shall be approved and filed with the competent authority.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Board shall convene an extraordinary meeting within 30 days to review the capital structure and to consider any further changes required for the commencement of business operations.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions taken by the officers of the Company prior to this meeting in connection with the incorporation process are hereby ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce - Online Name Reservation System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application via the MOEA online portal, providing the proposed company name in both Chinese and English, the intended business scope, and the proposed registered address. The name must not conflict with existing registered companies or trademarks. The application must be signed by the proposed incorporator or an authorized agent. Upon approval, the name is reserved for 30 days. Ensure the name includes 'Limited' or 'Co., Ltd.' as required by the Company Act. The process is straightforward and typically completed within 3 business days.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or national ID of the applicant
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to conflict, file an amended application within 15 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or a consent letter from the conflicting entity. If the rejection is based on non-compliance with naming rules, revise the name accordingly and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (IC-MOEA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for foreign investment approval, including the proposed business scope, capital amount, shareholder details, and a comprehensive business plan. The application must be accompanied by notarized certificates of incorporation of the foreign investor, audited financial statements for the last two years, and a power of attorney. The IC reviews the application for compliance with the Foreign Investment Act and any restrictions on the proposed business. Approval is typically granted within 30 days. Upon approval, the investor receives an Investment Approval Letter, which is a prerequisite for capital remittance and incorporation.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation of foreign investor
Audited financial statements of foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the IC's comments within 30 days. If rejected, file an appeal with the IC within 30 days, providing additional evidence or amendments to the business plan. Alternatively, revise the application and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any commercial bank in Taiwan (e.g., Bank of China, Cathay Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Approval Letter, open a temporary bank account in the name of the proposed company. The foreign investor must remit the capital contribution from abroad, and the bank will issue a capital remittance certificate. The funds must be deposited in the account and cannot be withdrawn until the company is formally registered. The bank will provide a certificate of deposit and a remittance certificate, which are essential for the incorporation registration. Ensure the remittance is properly documented and the source of funds is clear to comply with anti-money laundering regulations.
required_dossiers: Passport of the person opening the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation, provide the requested items promptly. If the remittance is delayed, obtain a letter from the foreign investor confirming the transfer and provide it to the bank. If the bank rejects the account opening, apply to another bank with the same documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce - Company Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation application to the MOEA, including the Articles of Incorporation, the name reservation certificate, the Investment Approval Letter, the capital remittance certificate, and the bank deposit certificate. The application must be signed by all directors and the supervisor. The MOEA will review the documents for compliance with the Company Act and issue a Certificate of Incorporation upon approval. The registration fee is calculated based on the authorized capital amount. The process typically takes 5-7 business days. Ensure all documents are notarized where required and translated into Chinese if originally in English.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors and supervisor
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, correct the deficiencies and resubmit within 30 days. If the rejection is based on substantive legal issues, file an appeal with the MOEA within 30 days, providing additional legal arguments or amendments to the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations (Tax, Labor, and Business Licenses)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration (for tax registration), Ministry of Labor (for labor registration), and local municipal government (for business license)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, register for corporate income tax, business tax, and withholding tax with the National Taxation Administration. Obtain a tax identification number (TIN). Register with the Ministry of Labor for labor insurance and pension contributions. Apply for a business license from the local municipal government if required. For legal services, no special industrial license is needed, but the company must comply with the Lawyers Act if it employs lawyers. Ensure all registrations are completed within 30 days of incorporation to avoid penalties.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact the tax office to expedite. If any registration is missing, provide the required documents and resubmit. If the business license is denied, appeal to the local government within 30 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan) and the local National Taxation Bureau at the company's registered address; official online portals: Ministry of Finance Tax Portal (https://www.tax.nat.gov.tw) and Electronic Uniform Invoice Integration Service Platform (https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Taiwan-incorporated WFOE obtains its statutory tax identifier (Unified Business Number, UBIN) automatically upon incorporation through the Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration System. The foreign parent/investor is not required to hold a Taiwanese TIN for the WFOE. The WFOE must (1) complete company registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs; (2) use the MOEA-issued UBIN as its TIN/VAT ID; (3) file profit-seeking enterprise income tax and business tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau before starting commercial operations; (4) apply for Uniform Invoice purchase authorization and, if electronic invoicing is adopted, join the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform; and (5) register as a withholding tax agent for employee salary and foreign payments. If the foreign parent itself makes taxable supplies in Taiwan without a Taiwan branch, it must obtain a non-resident business-tax registration number through the Ministry of Finance Tax Portal and appoint a local tax agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the WFOE is a Taiwan resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed on its own income; no pass-through treatment exists under Taiwan's Income Tax Act).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Taiwan has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election for a WFOE limited company; entity-level taxation is compulsory; only administrative elections such as electronic invoice filing mode are available).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax) enacted under the Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover threshold for a Taiwan-incorporated WFOE; tax registration is compulsory before commencing taxable business. For unincorporated small-scale businesses, simplified taxation applies when average monthly taxable sales are below NT$200,000, but that status is not available to a WFOE limited company.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the issuance of Uniform Invoices for all taxable sales. VAT-registered businesses must file Business Tax returns every two months and transmit electronic Uniform Invoice data to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform using the E-Invoice Turnkey API/EDI connectivity in the prescribed XML structure. Each electronic Uniform Invoice carries a tax-issued invoice code and an anti-counterfeit random code encoded in the QR/matrix barcode. There is no real-time prior fiscal clearance at the point of issuance; instead, the tax authority performs automated central-database cross-checks after transmission, and the taxpayer must retain the electronic invoice files and audit logs for the statutory records period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, a 0% Business Tax rate applies to the export of goods and to qualifying export-related services supplied for use or consumption entirely outside Taiwan, including cross-border commercial litigation advisory, arbitration and asset-tracing services delivered to an overseas recipient and not used in Taiwan. The claim is available only where the Taiwan entity retains contemporaneous evidence that legal title and risk passed overseas, the service recipient is outside Taiwan, and the proceeds are attributable to foreign currency receipts. Sales of digital services to Taiwan consumers are not zero-rated; such cross-border digital services become subject to 5% Business Tax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export customs declaration/electronic export entry issued by the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical export
Commercial Invoice, Packing List and the underlying export contract/purchase order
Foreign-exchange repatriation record (e.g., bank inward remittance advice, foreign exchange settlement slip, or Letter of Credit negotiation record)
For zero-rated services: a written service agreement, delivery/engagement records and recipient confirmation stating that the service is performed and consumed outside Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau and Customs Administration cross-match customs export declarations, e-invoice data and bank foreign-exchange receipt records. If the zero-rating substantiation bundle is incomplete, forged or untimely, or if export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory foreign-exchange deadline, the tax authority will reverse the zero-rated treatment, assess the 5% Business Tax, add delinquent interest, disallow any related input VAT credit or VAT refund, and impose monetary penalties in proportion to the tax evaded; intentional fraud or misrepresentation may further trigger criminal liability under Taiwan's tax collection laws.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBoC), together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), is the apex monetary and foreign exchange control authority for the mainland China banking system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under the Chinese foreign exchange regulatory framework, RMB is not fully convertible on the capital account. The current account (trade in goods and services, profits, dividends, interest, and wages) is largely convertible after furnishing authentic transaction documentation to the designated bank for verification. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment injections, outbound direct investment, cross-border loans, and equity transfers, require prior approval or registration with SAFE and are subject to periodic quotas and real-demand tests. Export proceeds in foreign currency are subject to the mandatory repatriation regime: Except for certain prudent exemptions, all export receipts must be repatriated into China and, while 100% may be retained on foreign exchange settlement accounts, the exporter's currency conversion is closely supervised, and any surplus above the account ceiling must be converted into RMB. Profit remittance by a WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder requires audited financial statements, completed annual corporate income tax filing, evidence of paid-in capital, and prior SAFE registration of the FDI capital injection. The bank will match the remitted amount to the verified distributable profit, and any mismatch triggers enhanced due diligence. Dividends are taxed under any applicable cross-strait or other double-taxation arrangement, and withholding tax certificates must be filed. Overall, the regime is administratively rigorous and stringent at the capital account level, while current account convertibility is achievable through documented, transparent transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE's current account administration, export proceeds must be repatriated into mainland China no later than 180 days after customs declaration (or a longer approved period) and must be credited to the enterprise's foreign exchange settlement account; there is no fixed compulsory conversion ratio to RMB, but the proceeds must pass through designated bank verification, and SAFE may mandate conversion of the balance above the enterprise's verified FX account ceiling. In practice, the mandatory surrender ratio is zero for legitimate export receipts, but repatriation, reporting in the Export Trade in Foreign Exchange Collection Confirmation system, and documentary authenticity review are strictly enforced.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Current Operating Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with cross-border trade settlement
Basic Operational Currency Account and export proceeds settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI providers such as Revolut, Wise Business, or Airwallex are not licensed as banks in mainland China and cannot hold a WFOE's primary corporate account, accept FDI capital injections, or clear CNH settlements through local clearing infrastructure. They may be used only as auxiliary foreign payment rails for non-regulated disbursements, provided funds do not touch domestic custody. Legal constraints under the PRC Banking Law and the E-CNY framework prohibit unlicensed deposit-taking and payment services; therefore, the viability rating is Very Low as a primary banking solution, and any deployment must be relegated to cross-border invoicing support via a licensed partner bank in Hong Kong or Singapore.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For WFOE corporate account opening with mainland Tier-1 banks, the legal representative (statutory director) must attend an in-branch interview for biometric and KYC verification; remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for the initial account relationship. Some pilot Free Trade Zone branches allow the legal representative to execute the opening via video-based e-KYC if the entity presents a notarized power of attorney and the individual's identity is independently verified by a Chinese consulate or overseas branch of the domestic bank, but the account activation is conditional upon subsequent in-branch signatory verification within a prescribed window.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity across the Taiwan/China cross-ownership chain, including nominee shareholders or holding entities in tax-neutral jurisdictions, raises suspicion of concealed owners and possible false disclosure under China's CDD regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete corporate ownership deed trail from the WFOE to the ultimate natural persons: certificate of incorporation for each entity, updated shareholder register, holders' passports with notarized translations, signed beneficial owner declaration under PBOC AML Rule No. 1/2019, and a detailed ledger of any nominee arrangements plus the underlying economic rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected large inbound credits to the IOLTA-adjacent trust or operating account from litigation funders or clients could be flagged as high-risk source-of-funds or potential money laundering through legal fees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a client engagement letter and fee agreement, a source-of-funds narrative with audited bank statements showing the initiating client accounts, a tax-compliant invoice or funding agreement, a trust ledger (IOLTA-style) proving segregated balances, and a legal opinion from PRC counsel confirming the litigation-funding structure does not violate PRC prohibitions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and politically exposed persons (PEP) overlap because cross-border commercial litigation may involve parties domiciled in sanctioned jurisdictions or have state-affiliated counterparties in mainland China or Taiwan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a sanctions-policy-compliant screening output with names of all counterparties and their ultimate owners, PEP classification forms, adverse-media reports in English, a sworn statement that no transaction touches US/EU/UN-sanctioned entities, and a legal engagement letter excluding representation of blocked persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-related disbursement mismatches when using SWIFT MT103 for litigation settlement payments may cause mismatched purpose codes or incorrect tariff classification, triggering SAFE export-import verification alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish the underlying tribunal award or court judgment, settlement agreement, an itemized disbursement schedule with the actual service scope under ISIC 6910, a completed SAFE Current Account Payment/Receipt Instruction with the correct foreign exchange purpose code, and a bank payment checklist evidencing the connection between the settlement amount and the litigation stage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a WFOE receiving equity capital from a Taiwan parent, the compliant route is: (i) obtain SAFE foreign investment registration (FDI) for the WFOE before any capital injection, generating a unique Foreign Exchange Business Registration Number; (ii) execute the inbound wire transfer from the Taiwan parent in foreign currency (e.g., USD) and remit to the WFOE's domestic Capital Account at a designated Tier-1 bank; (iii) ensure the SWIFT MT103 carries the SAFE BOPS transaction code category for direct investment in equity capital (purpose code 621012) and the benefactor name matches the registered investor; (iv) upon receipt, the bank verifies the inbound against the SAFE system, processes the capital verification declaration, and permits conversion to RMB for operating expenses only upon submission of payment orders to the bank; (v) a Chinese certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report confirming shareholder contribution before the company can record the capital as paid-in equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing options for outbound settlement payments from the WFOE include: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct remittances of invoices, settlement awards, and legal fees; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) for procurement of services or goods where the beneficiary requires a bank undertaking; (iii) Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) for lower-cost settlements with secured trade documents. Each payment must be initiated through a Tier-1 bank with a validated under-the-current-account transaction form, supported by the contract, invoice, financial statement, and, when above the threshold, the SAFE foreign exchange receipt/payment declaration form for BOPS statistical reporting. The bank will screen SWIFT messages for integrity, match the purpose code to the service or goods type, and block any transaction inconsistent with the registered business scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: SAFE-approved deliverable CNY forward contracts (requiring genuine current or capital account exposure)
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) registered with SAFE for long-term capital management
Onshore FX options (call/put) for hedging litigation receivables and settlement payables
Offshore CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are prohibited for the onshore WFOE; acceptable only through an offshore treasury affiliate under a direct economic hedge mandate

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% (profit-seeking enterprise income tax on taxable income exceeding NT$120,000; progressive 19% rate applies to the first tranche; national surtax abolished for retained earnings since 2018)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (15% of eligible expenditure, capped at 30% of current-year tax payable, 10-year carryforward); 5G/Smart Machinery investment credits (3%-5%); export-related and bilingual provisions not applicable; litigation chambers eligible only for general R&D/software investment credits.
